title.narrative: Albania Gender Equality in Access to Economic Opportunities DPF

description.narrative: The Program Development Objectives are to support the Government of Albania's efforts to enhance the policy framework for gender equality in access to economic opportunities, with a focus on (i) improving women's access to assets; (ii) leveling the playing field to enhance labor market opportunities for women; and (iii) strengthening institutional arrangements for gender-informed policy making.

The objectives of the Gender Equality in Access to Economic Opportunities Development Policy Financing Project for Albania are to support the Government of Albania's efforts to enhance the policy framework for gender equality in access to economic opportunities, with a focus on (i) improving women's access to assets, (ii) leveling the playing field to enhance labor market opportunities for women; and (iii) strengthening institutional arrangements for gender-informed policy making. Expected results include : Actions supported under Pillar 1 are expected to increase the accuracy of immovable property registries for married couples, improve the quality of information on property titles, and provide affordable legal assistance to ensure that property titles recognize the rights of vulnerable women. Prior Action 4 is an important first step towards mainstreaming gender in procurement in Albania and is expected to increase compliance with legislation on gender equality and nondiscrimination in employment practices, including the equal work for equal pay provisions of the Labor Code, and to strengthen respect for gender-equality principles in the private sector.

title.narrative: Percent of municipalities with an average teacher-student ratio in preschool less than or equal to 1:18

comment.narrative: <p>???????The original baseline and target were incorrectly stated, as in 2019 already 79% of municipalities had an average ratio of 18:1. By 2021 all municipalities had ratios below 18:1 and the change in rule has generally made funding of preschool more certain.  A significant reduction took place especially in Tirana and Ura Vajgurore.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of bidders in public procurement tenders that submit a self-declaration related to nondiscrimination in the workplace

comment.narrative: <p>The self-declaration form was very successfully introduced and so far, there has been a 100% compliance. Moreover, every 3 months PPA has shared the list of winners with the Labor Inspectorate (around 1,000 economic operators on average), which inspects about 40% of all winners and reports the cases where violations were identified, and corrections requested. During 2020, there was one case where an economic operator was found in violation of the labor code and took no corrective action; in 2021 six administrativeproceedings were initiated resulting in two dismissals, and four firms blacklisted for three years due to violation of the self-declaration on nondiscrimination. This prior action, mandating bidders to fill out the fields on nondiscrimination, was reinforcedwith its incorporation in a new Procurement law passed in 2020. In addition, the Labor Inspectorate has worked closely with the Public Procurement Authority (PPA) to confirm and enforce labor provisions.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of total records in the Albanian Digital Registry of Properties with a valid identification number and with the owners female gender verified

comment.narrative:
<p>No updated result is available as of May 2022, as the process of digitalization of <em>kartelas</em>??????? at the State Cadaster Office did not advance as planned. While the result was not achieved, there is substantial progress in this Pillar. At the time the DPF was prepared all three prior actions were expected to play a complementary role in increasing women’s claim on assets. Unfortunately, in 2019 only the cadaster action (PA 2) had a clear, measurable baseline on which to establish a results indicator. While the Cadaster Office has not made any appreciable progress in digitalizing property records and thus there is no new measureavailable, there has been notable progress on the implementation and institutionalization of PA 1 (Notary Law) and PA 3 (Legal Aid Law). Notaries are all trained on gender gaps and use the electronic system. The Legal Aid directorate is in place, as well as an M&E system for service delivery.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: Percent of budget programs across all line ministries that comply with the review process established by the gender responsive budgeting guidelines

comment.narrative: <p>While the target was not achieved in 2020, it was surpassed in 2021 and significantly surpassed in 2022. In March 2021 the Ministry of Finance provided a breakdown of the gender responsive budgeting (GRB) programs and KPIs for the 2021-2023 MTBP, showing that the number of GRB programs had reached its target of over half of the total budget programs, and a growing share of budget expenditure.  In the MTBP 2020-2022, 34 programs were identified as GRB; in the MTBP 2021-2023, 43 programs, and in the MTBP 2022-2024, 47 programs were identified as GRB. On the municipal side, all municipalities have received training for GRB identification and reporting (with support from UNWomen). </p>

title.narrative: Percent of women, including those categorized as vulnerable, that have been employed through the National Employment Services

comment.narrative: <p>Because of a gradual implementation of the new National Employment Services (NAES) and the deterioration of the labor market due to the pandemic, the share of registered women that were employed through NAES, which initially increased from 39% in 2018 to 48% in 2019, fell to 35% in 2020 and 31% in 2021. This was due to an increase in female registered jobseekers from 37 thousand in 2019 to 47 thousand in 2021 while the absolute number of placements declined from close to 15 thousand in 2019 to less than 12 thousand in 2021. In addition, the profile of ALMP beneficiaries shifted towards older workers in 2020 as the proportion of workers over 35 years old went from 29% in 2019 to 43% in 2020. Also of note, female beneficiaries of ALMPs fell by over 10% in 2020 before rising again in 2021.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of key performance indicators for gender responsive budgeting programs that directly address documented gender gaps in the country

comment.narrative: <p>The total number of key performance indicators (KPIs) substantially increased between 2019 and 2022 (from 39 to 91), while the number of KPIs effectively addressing gaps increased from 25 to 62. Thus, the share of KPIs addressing gender gaps fell from 80% (2020) to 75% (2021) and 68% (2022), but this is due to the substantial increase in total KPIs. One important challenge that continues to exist is the lack of sex-disaggregated data at the local level which limits the ability of local government to design and report on KPIs by gender.</p>
